title: 371. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Similarity Scaling of Area and Volume
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Square a linear scale factor to find an area factor.
questions.question: Two squares have side lengths \(3\text{ cm}\) and \(9\text{ cm}\). What is the larger square's area divided by the smaller square's area?
questions.explanation: The side ratio is \(3\), so the area ratio is \(3^2=9\).
questions.hint: Compare the side lengths before comparing areas.

questions.learningObjective: Cube a linear scale factor to find a volume factor.
questions.question: Two cubes have edge lengths \(3\text{ cm}\) and \(12\text{ cm}\). What is the larger cube's volume divided by the smaller cube's volume?
questions.explanation: The edge ratio is \(4\). Volume therefore scales by \(4^3=64\).
questions.hint: Count how many independent length dimensions contribute to volume.

questions.learningObjective: Infer area ratio from the perimeters of similar polygons.
questions.question: Two similar polygons have perimeter ratio \(2:5\), in the order smaller to larger. What is their area ratio in the same order?
questions.explanation: Similar polygons have the same perimeter and side-length ratios. Squaring \(2:5\) gives area ratio \(4:25\).
questions.hint: A perimeter ratio identifies the linear scale.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a surface-area ratio into a volume ratio for similar solids.
questions.question: Two similar solids have surface-area ratio \(9:16\). What is their volume ratio in the same order?
questions.explanation: The linear ratio is \(3:4\), so the volume ratio is \(3^3:4^3=27:64\).
questions.hint: Recover the linear ratio before using the volume relationship.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate area after a rational linear enlargement.
questions.question: A figure has area \(25\text{ cm}^2\). A similar image has every length multiplied by \(\frac{3}{2}\). What is the image's area?
questions.hint: Apply the scale factor to area, rather than directly to its numerical value.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate volume after a uniform reduction.
questions.question: A solid has volume \(375\text{ cm}^3\). A similar solid has every length multiplied by \(\frac{1}{5}\). What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume scales by the cube, giving \(375\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^3=3\text{ cm}^3\).
questions.hint: Determine the volume factor for a uniform length reduction.

questions.learningObjective: Recover a surface-area ratio from a volume ratio.
questions.question: Two similar solids have volume ratio \(125:8\). What is their surface-area ratio in the same order?
questions.explanation: Taking cube roots gives linear ratio \(5:2\). Squaring gives surface-area ratio \(25:4\).
questions.hint: Move from volume to length, then from length to area.

questions.learningObjective: Translate a percentage area increase into a volume factor.
questions.question: A solid is uniformly enlarged so its surface area increases by \(44\%\). What is the new volume divided by the original volume?
questions.explanation: The area factor is \(1.44=\frac{36}{25}\), so the length factor is \(\frac{6}{5}\). The volume factor is \(\left(\frac{6}{5}\right)^3=\frac{216}{125}\).
questions.hint: Convert the percentage to an area factor and recover its length factor.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a model volume using a stated linear scale.
questions.question: A solid model has linear scale \(1:20\) relative to the actual object and volume \(15\text{ cm}^3\). What is the actual object's volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.explanation: The actual-to-model length factor is \(20\). Thus the volume is \(15\cdot20^3=120000\text{ cm}^3\).
questions.hint: Interpret the scale as a length ratio before converting volume.

questions.learningObjective: Infer an area ratio from non-unit similar-solid volumes.
questions.question: Two similar solids have volumes \(54\text{ cm}^3\) and \(128\text{ cm}^3\). What is the second solid's surface area divided by the first solid's surface area?
questions.explanation: The volume ratio is \(\frac{128}{54}=\frac{64}{27}\). The linear factor is \(\frac{4}{3}\), so the surface-area factor is \(\frac{16}{9}\).
questions.hint: Reduce the volume ratio before taking its cube root.
